grand_strategy.reading: Papua New Guinea buys security from its partners (a mutual defence treaty with Australia in 2025, access for US forces since 2023) while its economy stays in foreign hands: LNG and nickel are run by foreign operators, and Chinese money finances the mines. The central constraint is Bougainville, whose independence can only be decided by a national parliament that has not yet voted. Not yet sourced in this first pass: tribal violence, state capacity, the Solomon Islands, Fiji, the Philippines, New Zealand, and the Ukraine and Gaza positions.

stances.note: Ally on the treaty reading: the Pukpuk Mutual Defence Treaty, signed 6 Oct 2025 in Canberra, treats an armed attack on either country as a danger to both, and it is the first alliance for PNG and Australia's first in more than 70 years. The sources read do not confirm entry into force; the joint communique says signature followed cabinet processes. Trend warming: the NRL franchise (about A$600 million over ten years) and police support run alongside. Bond affinity: no open grievance found in the sources read. Confidence B: the communique is tier 1 but the signing details come from press reports.

It is described as Australia's first alliance in more than 70 years and only the third, after the US and New Zealand. It entered into force in July 2026 (AAP report of 9 Jul, at the leaders' dialogue in Brisbane); the PNG card, written earlier, says entry into force was not confirmed. Trend warming: the NRL franchise (about A$600m over ten years) and police support run alongside. Bond - affinity: no open grievance found in the sources read.
